current_events: Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez says that the United Nations' International Maritime Organization will pause an evacuation effort for 11,000 seafarers on stranded ships in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran objected to the plan and after a vessel was attacked near Oman

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy rejects the UN- and Omani-proposed plan, stating that passage is only permitted through the routes approved by Iran, and that it will take action against ships violating instructions

Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely is damaged after being struck by a unknown projectile off the coast of Oman, near Dahit in the Musandam Governorate. A United States official tells MS NOW that Iran was behind the attack. No casualties are reported
2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
Omani foreign minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi confirms that no transit fees would be imposed on ships using the Strait of Hormuz as part of future management of the waterway

Two liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers from Qatar, the Marshall Islands-flagged Bu Samra bound for the Far East and Liberia-flagged Patris, transit through the Strait of Hormuz after being stranded for a period of time since the waterway was closed
Israel and Lebanon deny a claim from a US official that some Israeli troops have been withdrawn from southern Lebanon as a goodwill gesture during their negotiations
Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that the Israeli military will keep troops in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza indefinitely

Two people were killed and seven others were injured in a drone strike by the paramilitary group Rapid Support Forces on a fuel station in Rabak, White Nile in the southern region of Sudan. The Sudan Doctors Network confirms the attack in a statement
French president Emmanuel Macron announces that the French Navy intercepted and boarded the Cameroon-flagged, Russia-linked oil tanker Deliver off the coast of Sicily two days earlier

The Federal Reserve inflation rises to a three-year high in May. Additionally, the U.S. Department of Commerce reported a 4.1% increase in consumer prices driven by high gas prices, the largest since April 2023

Reuters reports that over the past week crude oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have risen to their highest level since the start of the war, but traffic still remains a fraction of pre-war levels
Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
The confirmed toll of yesterday's earthquakes in Venezuela rises to 188 people killed, over 1000 people injured, and more than 36,000 others believed to be missing
Two people are killed and another is injured in a plane crash in Warsaw, Poland
At least two are injured after two trains collide near Piła, Poland
A monitoring system in Spain estimates that a heat wave contributed to 212 deaths between Sunday and Wednesday. The country also records its highest average June temperatures since at least 1950
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis confirms that the Alligator Alcatraz detention center in Ochopee, Florida, U.S., will close operations, a year after it opened
Immigration detention in the second Trump administration
King's Representative Tom Marsters dissolves the Parliament of the Cook Islands, setting an election for 12 August 2026
2026 Cook Islands general election

The Congress of Deputies approves a motion calling on the Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to face a vote of confidence following the escalation of corruption cases involving his ruling PSOE party and Sánchez's family
Ivory Coast's soccer team reaches the knockout stage of the FIFA World Cup for the first time in its team history, defeating Curaçao, 2-0, in Group E
Ivory Coast at the FIFA World Cup
